contents.name: Chapter 10 introduction, equations (10.4)–(10.5): gradient and Hessian of one-half the squared residual norm
contents.reason: The assigned theorem states and proves both identities, retaining the residual-curvature term and its zero-residual special case.

contents.name: §10.1, Example 10.1: nonlinear measurement model represented by a residual vector and sum of squares
contents.reason: The B-page fit explicitly defines two observation residuals, evaluates an exact fit, and verifies the Jacobian rank.

contents.name: §10.2: full-rank linear least squares by reduced QR and SVD, avoiding explicit normal-equation solves
contents.reason: The assigned algorithm specifies exact QR/SVD branches, does not form J^T J, and records computed status limits.

contents.name: §10.2, equations (10.19)–(10.22): SVD sensitivity and the family of minimizers for rank-deficient data
contents.reason: The B-page rank-deficient example computes a one-dimensional family of exact minimizers and separates this from the unique damped solve.

contents.name: §10.3, equations (10.23)–(10.27): Gauss-Newton normal system as the linearized least-squares subproblem
contents.reason: The assigned algorithm proves that its exact full-rank QR/SVD branches minimize the linearized residual problem.

contents.name: §10.3, Theorem 10.1: global gradient convergence for a Wolfe line-search Gauss-Newton method
contents.reason: The source theorem assumes a line search and Wolfe-type step conditions; this batch instead proves a local exact-step contraction and a separate finite-budget LM stationarity result, so it does not build this global line-search theorem.

contents.name: §10.3, equation (10.30): local Gauss-Newton error estimate and the zero-residual quadratic special case
contents.reason: The local theorem derives an explicit contraction from residual curvature; the companion theorem proves the quadratic recurrence when the residual vanishes.

contents.name: §10.3, Lemma 10.2: trust-region optimality characterization of a Levenberg-Marquardt step
contents.reason: The local lemma proves the scaled trust-region minimization directly from the damped positive-definite normal system.

contents.name: §10.3, equations (10.35), (10.39)–(10.41): augmented least-squares form and ellipsoidal scaling
contents.reason: The LM algorithm uses the augmented matrix [J; sqrt(lambda)D] and spells out the trust-radius and ratio status branches.

contents.name: §10.3, Theorem 10.3: global LM stationarity under the source’s Cauchy-decrease condition
contents.reason: The source theorem is for approximate trust-region steps satisfying a separate Cauchy-decrease lower bound; the assigned global item proves a distinct exact-solve, finite-rejection statement and does not claim this source theorem’s proof.

contents.name: §10.3, “Methods for large-residual problems”: asymptotic Gauss-Newton and LM convergence may be only linear
contents.reason: The B-page scalar residual gives a fully computed nonzero-residual stationary point with a limiting linear factor and no quadratic bound.

contents.name: §10.3, hybrid Gauss-Newton/quasi-Newton algorithms for large-residual problems
contents.reason: The hybrid updates require a separate Hessian-approximation algorithm and are outside the assigned GN/LM scope; no hybrid method or rate is claimed in these items.

item_arguments.argument: Expand the squared residual coordinatewise, differentiate using the product and chain rules, and identify the Jacobian Gram term plus residual-weighted component Hessians.
Apply vector FTC along the segment, subtract the endpoint Jacobian term, and integrate the Lipschitz bound L(1-t)||e||² to obtain L||e||²/2 for rectangular maps.
Use z=Dp and positive definiteness of J^TJ+lambda D^TD to prove unique damped minimization, then compare penalized and unregularized objectives on the induced ball.
Give finite QR/SVD exact and computed branches with explicit rank/status outcomes; prove exact full-rank minimization and restrict backward stability to its supplier hypotheses.
Form the augmented least-squares system, check positive prediction before ratios, apply explicit domain/radius/ratio branches, and cap attempts.
Integrate the gradient from stationary x*, bound variation of J^TJ and residual curvature, and multiply by the inverse Gram bound 1/sigma² to get q.
Use the rectangular residual remainder and least-squares orthogonality to bound the step error by L||e||²/(2sigma), then prove invariance under the stated radius.
Derive explicit bounds for step size, radius, model error and predicted reduction; choose Lambda so |rho-1|≤1-eta2 and count geometric rejections.
Combine finite acceptance, compact-sublevel invariance, bounded damping and a uniform decrease by ||J^Tr||²; telescope and pass to accumulation points by continuity.
Differentiate the two residuals, evaluate the exact root, and show its two-by-two Jacobian determinant is nonzero before identifying the exact GN step.
Compute rank one and the line of undamped minimizers; solve the damped two-by-two system and verify prediction, ratio, feasibility, and acceptance.
Derive the exact scalar GN recurrence, show iterates contract to a stationary point with nonzero residual, verify the local theorem hypotheses, and compare first- and second-order error ratios.
